one_line: Kerala temple-service scholar of the Tantrasangraha tradition, commentator on mathematics and astronomy in the 16th century.

appearance.age_look: early 40s, slender, slightly stooped from long hours of study
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown Kerala complexion, sharp nose, thin lips, neatly trimmed moustache, thoughtful eyes with a calm, analytic gaze; default expression is gentle seriousness with a hint of curiosity
appearance.hair: black hair, oiled and parted at the center, drawn back into a small low knot at the nape rather than a topknot; simple thin horizontal sandalwood tilak on the forehead; no turban, only a plain off‑white cotton headband tied around the crown
appearance.costume: simple Kerala scholar’s attire: a cream‑white cotton mundu (dhoti) wrapped from waist to ankles with a narrow golden kasavu border, pleats falling straight in front; upper body covered with a thin off‑white cotton uttariya drape over both shoulders and chest, with one end folded neatly over the left arm; no heavy jewellery, only a single small tulsi bead necklace and a copper wrist bangle on the right hand; bare feet but modestly covered by the long mundu; textiles are plain, slightly textured hand‑woven cotton without patterns, emphasizing temple‑service simplicity and scholarly focus.
appearance.signature: a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle of Yukti‑dīpikā tied with a dark cord in his left hand, and in the right a slender stylus for inscribing on palm leaves, held like a precise instrument.

ref_desc: Śaṅkara Variyar is a medium‑brown, slender Kerala scholar with black hair tied in a low knot and a sandal paste tilak, wearing a cream‑white kasavu‑border mundu and uttariya, carrying a palm‑leaf manuscript bundle and stylus in warm cream, gold, brown, and black tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character of Śaṅkara Variyar, a 16th‑century Kerala temple‑service scholar: medium‑brown skin, oval face, calm serious eyes, thin moustache, black hair oiled and center‑parted, pulled into a small low knot at the nape, with a simple thin horizontal sandalwood tilak on his forehead and a plain off‑white cotton headband around his crown. He wears an era‑accurate cream‑white cotton mundu (dhoti) reaching the ankles with a narrow golden kasavu border, pleated neatly in front, and a thin off‑white cotton uttariya (upper cloth) draped over both shoulders and across his chest, one end folded over his left forearm. His feet are bare but modestly covered by the long mundu; jewellery is minimal, just a small tulsi bead necklace and a copper wrist bangle on his right hand. In his left hand he holds a tightly bound bundle of palm‑leaf manuscripts representing Yukti‑dīpikā, tied with a dark cord, and in his right hand a slender stylus for writing on palm leaves, gripped with precise, deliberate control. Use a simple, dignified colour scheme of cream white for garments, warm golden for borders and bangle, medium brown for skin and palm leaves, dark brown for cord and stylus, and black for hair and headband, presented as a clear model sheet showing front view, full costume, hairstyle, and signature manuscript and stylus for consistent redrawing.
